facts.statement: The genus Biropristis was named to honor Dr. Lajos Biró-Bagózcky, who studied the geological formation where the fossils were discovered.
facts.quote: The genus is named in honor of Dr. Lajos Biró-Bagózcky who studied the formation in which it was found.

facts.statement: The only known fossils of Biropristis are isolated oral teeth discovered in the Maastrichtian-aged Quiriquina Formation in central Chile.
facts.quote: It is known solely from isolated oral teeth found in the Maastrichtian-aged Quiriquina Formation of central Chile.

facts.statement: The species B. landbecki is named after Luis Landbeck, who discovered the first fossils at the specific locality.
facts.quote: The species is named for Luis Landbeck who found the first fossils at the locality in which it was found.

facts.statement: Biropristis is an extinct genus of sclerorhynchoid that lived during the Late Cretaceous epoch.
facts.quote: Biropristis is an extinct genus of sclerorhynchoid from the Late Cretaceous epoch of the Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The genus Biropristis belongs to the family Sclerorhynchidae.
Biropristis is classified within the class Chondrichthyes, which includes cartilaginous fish.
Biropristis lived between 83.6 and 66 million years ago, spanning from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)
